change_policy: Changes must be mirrored in key-facts.md and recorded in the decision log. The standard is not adjusted after seeing model answers.

verdict_categories.missing_bonus: A bonus fact is absent. Recorded; does not affect the pass.
verdict_categories.insufficient_required: A required fact is absent or the question's minimum is not met. Fail.
verdict_categories.factual_error: The answer contains a listed error, a statement contradicting the paper, or a number not in the paper. Fail; counted separately.
verdict_categories.citation_not_supporting: A cited page does not contain the claim, or a number in the answer is not on any cited page (AC-26). Fail; counted separately.

common_rules: Every claim carries a source index (AC-05).
The answer is in the language of the question; Chinese questions are answered in Traditional Chinese.
Values in Table 1 and Table 2 are pairwise win rates (an LLM judge picks one of two answers), not model accuracy. Calling them accuracy is a factual error.
paper_quirks: Page 9, section 4.5: the cost comparison (tokens and API calls) is Figure 2, a table rendered as a figure, but the text says 'presented in Table 2'. Table 2 is the ablation study on page 8. Cost numbers (610,000; 1,399; 5,000; <100) are not ablation results.

questions.question: summary this document.

required.fact: Problem: existing RAG relies on flat data representations and lacks contextual awareness, giving fragmented answers
required.evidence: existing RAG systems have significant limitations, including reliance on flat data representations and inadequate contextual awareness

required.fact: Method: LightRAG incorporates graph structures into text indexing and retrieval
required.evidence: we propose LightRAG, which incorporates graph structures into text indexing and retrieval processes

required.fact: Core: dual-level retrieval, low-level (entities, relations) and high-level (topics, themes)
Incremental update without rebuilding the whole index
required.evidence: an incremental update algorithm that ensures the timely integration of new data

required.fact: Result: names at least one concrete comparison dimension (Comprehensiveness, Diversity, Empowerment, Overall, retrieval cost) or comparison target (NaiveRAG, RQ-RAG, HyDE, GraphRAG); 'performs better' alone is not enough
required.evidence: Extensive experimental validation demonstrates considerable improvements in retrieval accuracy and efficiency; Table 1; the cost comparison on page 9
required.rule: At least one keyword from keywords_any must be present and used as a comparison; a bare 'better than existing methods' fails this fact.

bonus.fact: Graph structures combined with vector representations
bonus.evidence: the integration of graph structures with vector representations

bonus.fact: Four datasets (Agriculture, CS, Legal, Mix) and four dimensions compared as pairwise win rates
Retrieval cost: LightRAG under 100 tokens and 1 API call vs GraphRAG about 610,000 tokens
bonus.evidence: Figure 2 and the text on page 9
We have made our LightRAG open-source

bonus.fact: Three challenges: comprehensive retrieval, retrieval efficiency, rapid adaptation to new data

factual_errors.text: Attributing cited works (R-Eval, GraphRAG, RQ-RAG, HyDE) to this paper
factual_errors.check: manual; flag 'R-Eval'/'R-eval' described as proposed by the paper

factual_errors.text: Claiming LightRAG leads in every case (on Mix, GraphRAG wins three dimensions; 'better overall' is correct, 'leads everywhere' is not)
factual_errors.check: manual; flag '所有'/'全面'/'all datasets'/'every' applied to superiority

factual_errors.text: Numbers or conclusions not in the paper

insufficient_examples: Covers only the problem and method without results, or only the results

questions.question: compare lightRAG with GraphRAG
questions.rule: A difference counts only if it compares the two methods on a stated aspect (what each does or scores). 'LightRAG is better' or 'GraphRAG is slower' without an aspect does not count. Numbers, when used, must be correct.

required.fact: Both graph-based; LightRAG has the higher win rate overall, especially on the larger Agriculture, CS and Legal datasets
required.evidence: LightRAG consistently outperforms GraphRAG, particularly in larger datasets with complex language contexts

required.fact: LightRAG's clearest advantage is Diversity, attributed to dual-level retrieval
required.evidence: LightRAG demonstrates a significant advantage in the Diversity metric

required.fact: Retrieval cost (Figure 2): GraphRAG 1,399 communities, 610 level-2 used, ~1,000 tokens each, ~610,000 tokens, hundreds of API calls; LightRAG under 100 tokens, one API call
Incremental update: GraphRAG dismantles and regenerates communities, about 1,399 x 2 x 5,000 tokens; LightRAG integrates new entities and relations without full reconstruction
required.evidence: GraphRAG must dismantle its existing community structure

required.fact: Mechanism: GraphRAG traverses community reports (brute-force); LightRAG uses dual-level retrieval over graph and vector representations
required.evidence: existing methods often rely on brute-force searches for each generated community

bonus.fact: Table 1 Overall win rates GraphRAG vs LightRAG: Agriculture 45.2/54.8, CS 48.0/52.0, Legal 47.2/52.8, Mix 50.4/49.6
Exception: on Mix, GraphRAG slightly wins Comprehensiveness (50.4/49.6), Empowerment (50.8/49.2) and Overall (50.4/49.6)
Case study (Table 3): the LLM judge prefers LightRAG on all four dimensions
bonus.evidence: LightRAG outperforms in all evaluation dimensions assessed by the LLM judge

bonus.fact: Similar extraction overhead for both during incremental updates
bonus.evidence: both models exhibit similar overhead for entity and relationship extraction

factual_errors.text: Claiming LightRAG beats GraphRAG on every dataset and every dimension; 'better overall' or 'wins on most datasets' is correct and is not this error
factual_errors.check: manual; only 'all'/'every'/'所有'/'全面' claims count

factual_errors.text: Using NaiveRAG, RQ-RAG or HyDE numbers as GraphRAG's
factual_errors.check: numbers verified against the GraphRAG block of Table 1

factual_errors.text: Presenting Table 1 win rates as model accuracy
factual_errors.check: manual; flag '準確率'/'accuracy' applied to the win rates

factual_errors.text: Comparisons the paper does not make

insufficient_examples: Only vague superiority statements without a comparison aspect

questions.question: Performance of ablated versions of LightRAG
questions.rule: (a) Explain what each of -High, -Low and -Origin removes and its main observation (A1-A5). (b) For at least one dataset and one metric, give the numbers of all four of LightRAG, -High, -Low and -Origin, each matching its Table 2 cell (A6). Numbers without analysis, or analysis without numbers, is insufficient.

required.fact: -High removes high-level retrieval (low-level only); -Low removes low-level (high-level only); -Origin removes original text from retrieval
-High: significant decline across nearly all datasets and metrics; too focused on entities and immediate neighbours
required.evidence: leading to a significant performance decline across nearly all datasets and metrics

required.fact: -Low: advantage in comprehensiveness, less depth on specific entities
required.evidence: offers a significant advantage in comprehensiveness

required.fact: -Origin: no significant decline; better than the full version on some datasets and metrics (the paper names Agriculture and Mix); graph indexing already captured key information, original text adds noise
required.evidence: does not exhibit significant performance declines across all four datasets

required.fact: Full (hybrid) LightRAG combines both levels: breadth and depth, balanced performance
required.evidence: The hybrid mode, or the full version of LightRAG

required.fact: For one dataset and one metric, all four variants' numbers, each exactly matching its Table 2 cell
required.rule: Find a (dataset, metric) pair for which the answer states values for LightRAG, -High, -Low and -Origin; all four must equal the Table 2 cells.

bonus.fact: Table 2 reports pairwise win rates against NaiveRAG over four datasets and four dimensions
Numbers for more than one dataset or metric, all matching Table 2

factual_errors.check: every percentage must be a Table 2 value

factual_errors.check: flag those numbers in a Q3 answer
